verses.text: Who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?

xrefs.text: This was to fulfill the word of Isaiah the prophet: “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”
But not all of them welcomed the good news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our message?”
For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
But to all who did receive Him, to those who believed in His name, He gave the right to become children of God—
Jesus replied, “Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah! For this was not revealed to you by flesh and blood, but by My Father in heaven.

verses.text: He grew up before Him like a tender shoot, and like a root out of dry ground. He had no stately form or majesty to attract us, no beauty that we should desire Him.

xrefs.text: Who, existing in the form of God, did not consider equality with God something to be grasped,
Just as many were appalled at Him His appearance was disfigured beyond that of any man, and His form was marred beyond human likeness —
He was in the world, and though the world was made through Him, the world did not recognize Him.
Then a shoot will spring up from the stump of Jesse, and a Branch from his roots will bear fruit.
Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Aren’t His sisters here with us as well? And they took offense at Him.

verses.text: He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief. Like one from whom men hide their faces, He was despised, and we esteemed Him not.

xrefs.text: He was in the world, and though the world was made through Him, the world did not recognize Him.
Then they spit in His face and struck Him. Others slapped Him
Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy set before Him endured the cross, scorning its shame, and sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

Yet it was the LORD’s will to crush Him and to cause Him to suffer; and when His soul is made a guilt offering, He will see His offspring, He will prolong His days, and the good pleasure of the LORD will prosper in His hand.

Thus says the LORD, the Redeemer and Holy One of Israel, to Him who was despised and abhorred by the nation, to the Servant of rulers: “Kings will see You and rise, and princes will bow down, because of the LORD, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen You.”

verses.text: Surely He took up our infirmities and carried our sorrows; yet we considered Him stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.

xrefs.text: He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree, so that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. “By His stripes you are healed.”
This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah: “He took up our infirmities and carried our diseases.”
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree.”
He Himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the sins of the whole world.
For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit,

verses.text: But He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that brought us peace was upon Him, and by His stripes we are healed.

xrefs.text: He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree, so that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. “By His stripes you are healed.”
For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit,
just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.
God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.
For at just the right time, while we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.

verses.text: We all like sheep have gone astray, each one has turned to his own way; and the LORD has laid upon Him the iniquity of us all.

xrefs.text: For “you were like sheep going astray,” but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit,
I have strayed like a lost sheep; seek Your servant, for I have not forgotten Your commandments.
Let the wicked man forsake his way and the unrighteous man his thoughts; let him return to the LORD, that He may have compassion, and to our God, for He will freely pardon.
He was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification.

verses.text: He was oppressed and afflicted, yet He did not open His mouth. He was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is silent, so He did not open His mouth.

xrefs.text: The eunuch was reading this passage of Scripture: “He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before the shearer is silent, so He did not open His mouth.
But Jesus remained silent. Then the high priest said to Him, “I charge You under oath by the living God: Tell us if You are the Christ, the Son of God.
When they heaped abuse on Him, He did not retaliate; when He suffered, He made no threats, but entrusted Himself to Him who judges justly.
But Jesus remained silent and made no reply. Again the high priest questioned Him, “Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?
and he went back into the Praetorium. “Where are You from? he asked. But Jesus gave no answer.

verses.text: By oppression and judgment He was taken away, and who can recount His descendants? For He was cut off from the land of the living; He was stricken for the transgression of My people.

xrefs.text: For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit,
In His humiliation He was deprived of justice. Who can recount His descendants? For His life was removed from the earth.”
“We have a law, answered the Jews, “and according to that law He must die, because He declared Himself to be the Son of God.
At this, the high priest tore his clothes and declared, “He has blasphemed! Why do we need any more witnesses? Look, now you have heard the blasphemy.
Many bulls surround me; strong bulls of Bashan encircle me.

verses.text: He was assigned a grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in His death, although He had done no violence, nor was any deceit in His mouth.

xrefs.text: When it was evening, there came a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph, who himself was a disciple of Jesus.
“He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in His mouth.”
But you know that Christ appeared to take away sins, and in Him there is no sin.
Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent Council member who himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, boldly went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.
God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.

verses.text: Yet it was the LORD’s will to crush Him and to cause Him to suffer; and when His soul is made a guilt offering, He will see His offspring, He will prolong His days, and the good pleasure of the LORD will prosper in His hand.

xrefs.text: God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.
He who did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, freely give us all things?
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree.”

Awake, O sword, against My Shepherd, against the man who is My Companion, declares the LORD of Hosts. Strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered, and I will turn My hand against the little ones.
He predestined us for adoption as His sons through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of His will,

verses.text: After the anguish of His soul, He will see the light of life and be satisfied. By His knowledge My righteous Servant will justify many, and He will bear their iniquities.

xrefs.text: So then, just as one trespass brought condemnation for all men, so also one act of righteousness brought justification and life for all men.
Surely He took up our infirmities and carried our sorrows; yet we considered Him stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.
He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree, so that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. “By His stripes you are healed.”

And they sang a new song: “Worthy are You to take the scroll and open its seals, because You were slain, and by Your blood You purchased for God those from every tribe and tongue and people and nation.
For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit,

verses.text: Therefore I will allot Him a portion with the great, and He will divide the spoils with the strong, because He has poured out His life unto death, and He was numbered with the transgressors. Yet He bore the sin of many and made intercession for the transgressors.

xrefs.text: For I tell you that this Scripture must be fulfilled in Me: ‘And He was numbered with the transgressors.’ For what is written about Me is reaching its fulfillment.
so also Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many; and He will appear a second time, not to bear sin, but to bring salvation to those who eagerly await Him.
Two others, who were criminals, were also led away to be executed with Jesus.
Along with Jesus, they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.
I am writing to you, little children, because your sins have been forgiven through His name.
